rules: Read the paragraph and the cited source before judging.
Before judging, state what the claim is meant to say, using the surrounding paragraph.
List implied propositions the paragraph attaches to the claim (mark origin: context).
Split the claim into sub-claims and judge each against the source separately.
Different wording is not a reason to lower a rating when the meaning is the same.
Judge only what the cited source says, not whether the claim is true in general.
Evidence quotes must be exact, with a location. If none exists, return absent.
If the source cannot be read, return source_unavailable. Never guess.
If the claim is a quote, ensure the quote is copied word for word from the source
